title: Data, operator, discretization, and solve errors

items.title: Error budget for computed Tikhonov inversion

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, arXiv:2001.00617v2, Chapter 8
Per Christian Hansen, Introduction to Inverse Problems, Chapter 5: Regularization Parameter Choice
Tristan van Leeuwen and Christoph Brune, 10 Lectures on Inverse Problems and Imaging, Chapter 3

items.statement:
Let $X,Y$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces over the same scalar field, let
$A:X\to Y$ be a compact linear forward map (the closure of $A(B)$ is compact
in $Y$ for every bounded set $B\subseteq X$), and let $A_h:X\to Y$ be a
bounded linear discretized map with finite-dimensional range. For a datum
$b\in Y$, let $\lambda>0$ be the coefficient of $\|x\|_X^2$ in the Tikhonov
objective $\|Ax-b\|_Y^2+\lambda\|x\|_X^2$. Supply adjoints $A^*:Y\to X$ and
$A_h^*:Y\to X$ satisfying
$\langle Ax,y\rangle_Y=\langle x,A^*y\rangle_X$ and
$\langle A_hx,y\rangle_Y=\langle x,A_h^*y\rangle_X$, where the inner products
are linear in their first arguments. Assume the shifted normal operators
$A^*A+\lambda I_X$ and $A_h^*A_h+\lambda I_X$ are bijective, and define
$$R_\lambda=(A^*A+\lambda I_X)^{-1}A^*,\qquad R_{\lambda,h}=(A_h^*A_h+\lambda I_X)^{-1}A_h^*.$$

For a truth $x^\dagger\in X$, data perturbation $e\in Y$, and $\delta\ge0$
with $\|e\|\le\delta$, put
$$y=Ax^\dagger,\qquad y_\delta=y+e,\qquad y_{h,\delta}=A_hx^\dagger+e,\qquad d_h=(A-A_h)x^\dagger=y_\delta-y_{h,\delta}.$$
For any returned output $\widetilde x_h\in X$, define its exact discrete
normal-equation residual by
$$r_{h,h}=(A_h^*A_h+\lambda I_X)\widetilde x_h-A_h^*y_{h,\delta}.$$
The five-channel error budget is the ordered tuple
$(b_{\mathrm{bias}},b_{\mathrm{data}},b_{\mathrm{operator}},b_{\mathrm{pre}},b_{\mathrm{solve}})$, where
$$\begin{aligned}b_{\mathrm{bias}}&=x^\dagger-R_\lambda y,\qquad b_{\mathrm{data}}=R_\lambda y-R_\lambda y_\delta,\\b_{\mathrm{operator}}&=(R_\lambda-R_{\lambda,h})y_{h,\delta},\qquad b_{\mathrm{pre}}=R_\lambda d_h,\\b_{\mathrm{solve}}&=R_{\lambda,h}y_{h,\delta}-\widetilde x_h.\end{aligned}$$
The five entries are, in order, the truth-bias, data-perturbation,
regularized-operator, pre-inversion, and algebraic-solve error vectors.
The scalar total budget is the sum of the five channel norms. The raw
pre-inversion forward residual is $d_h$; its reconstruction contribution is
$b_{\mathrm{pre}}$. The operator channel measures the difference between the
regularized exact and discretized operators. The solve channel measures the
returned output's difference from the exact discrete Tikhonov output. The
definition supplies no rate or arithmetic residual certificate.

items.title: Regularized output error splits into source-specific terms

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, arXiv:2001.00617v2, Chapter 8
Per Christian Hansen, Introduction to Inverse Problems, Chapter 5: Regularization Parameter Choice
Tristan van Leeuwen and Christoph Brune, 10 Lectures on Inverse Problems and Imaging, Chapter 3

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, meaning every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice
function. Let $X,Y$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces over the same scalar
field, let $A:X\to Y$ be compact and linear (the closure of $A(B)$ is compact
in $Y$ for every bounded set $B\subseteq X$), and let $A_h:X\to Y$ be bounded
and linear with finite-dimensional range. Let $A^*:Y\to X$ and $A_h^*:Y\to X$
be their Hilbert adjoints, characterized by
$\langle Ax,z\rangle_Y=\langle x,A^*z\rangle_X$ and
$\langle A_hx,z\rangle_Y=\langle x,A_h^*z\rangle_X$, with both inner
products linear in the first argument. Let $\lambda>0$, $x^\dagger\in X$,
$e\in Y$, $\delta\ge0$ with $\|e\|_Y\le\delta$, and
$\widetilde x_h\in X$. Put
$$y=Ax^\dagger,\qquad y_\delta=y+e,\qquad y_{h,\delta}=A_hx^\dagger+e,\qquad d_h=(A-A_h)x^\dagger=y_\delta-y_{h,\delta}.$$
$$R_\lambda=(A^*A+\lambda I_X)^{-1}A^*,\qquad R_{\lambda,h}=(A_h^*A_h+\lambda I_X)^{-1}A_h^*,$$
where $I_X$ is the identity operator on $X$, and
$$r_{h,h}=(A_h^*A_h+\lambda I_X)\widetilde x_h-A_h^*y_{h,\delta}.$$
Define
$$\begin{aligned}b_{\mathrm{bias}}&=x^\dagger-R_\lambda y,&b_{\mathrm{data}}&=R_\lambda y-R_\lambda y_\delta,\\b_{\mathrm{operator}}&=(R_\lambda-R_{\lambda,h})y_{h,\delta},&b_{\mathrm{pre}}&=R_\lambda d_h,\\b_{\mathrm{solve}}&=R_{\lambda,h}y_{h,\delta}-\widetilde x_h.\end{aligned}$$
Then the exact error identity and its triangle bound are
$$x^\dagger-\widetilde x_h=b_{\mathrm{bias}}+b_{\mathrm{data}}+b_{\mathrm{pre}}+b_{\mathrm{operator}}+b_{\mathrm{solve}},$$
$$\|x^\dagger-\widetilde x_h\|\le \|b_{\mathrm{bias}}\|+\|b_{\mathrm{data}}\|+\|b_{\mathrm{pre}}\|+\|b_{\mathrm{operator}}\|+\|b_{\mathrm{solve}}\|,$$
and the four displayed term estimates give
$$\|x^\dagger-\widetilde x_h\|\le \|b_{\mathrm{bias}}\|+\frac{\delta}{2\sqrt\lambda}+\frac{\|d_h\|}{2\sqrt\lambda}+\|b_{\mathrm{operator}}\|+\frac{\|r_{h,h}\|}{\lambda}.$$
If $\|R_\lambda-R_{\lambda,h}\|_{Y\to X}\le\eta_{\lambda,h}$, where the
induced operator norm for a bounded linear map $T:Y\to X$ is
$$\|T\|_{Y\to X}:=\sup_{u\in Y,\,\|u\|_Y\le1}\|Tu\|_X,$$
then
$\|b_{\mathrm{operator}}\|\le\eta_{\lambda,h}\|y_{h,\delta}\|_Y$. If a
residual evaluation separately supplies $\widehat r_{h,h}\in X$ and
$\rho_{h,h}\ge0$ with
$\|\widehat r_{h,h}-r_{h,h}\|_X\le\rho_{h,h}$, then the final solve term is at
most $(\|\widehat r_{h,h}\|_X+\rho_{h,h})/\lambda$. These pointwise bounds assert
no convergence rate as the data, regularization parameter, or discretization
changes.

title: Data, operator, discretization, and solve errors — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Vanishing data errors with persistent small-singular-value reconstruction error

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, arXiv:2001.00617v2, Chapter 8
Per Christian Hansen, Introduction to Inverse Problems, Chapter 5: Regularization Parameter Choice
Tristan van Leeuwen and Christoph Brune, 10 Lectures on Inverse Problems and Imaging, Chapter 3

items.statement:
For every integer $n\ge1$, let $X_n=Y_n=\mathbb R^n$ with the Euclidean
inner product and let
$$A_n=A_{h,n}=\operatorname{diag}(1,1/2,\ldots,1/n).$$
Set $x_n^\dagger=0$, exact data $y_n=A_nx_n^\dagger=0$, noise
$e_n=(0,\ldots,0,1/n)$, noise bound $\delta_n=1/n$, and regularization
coefficient $\lambda_n=n^{-4}$. The observed data are
$y_{n,\delta}=y_n+e_n$, and the returned output is the exact Tikhonov output
$$\widetilde x_n=(A_n^*A_n+\lambda_n I)^{-1}A_n^*y_{n,\delta}.$$
The smallest singular value of $A_n$ is $1/n$, while
$\|e_n\|=\delta_n\to0$. Nevertheless
$$\|\widetilde x_n-x_n^\dagger\|=\frac{n^2}{n^2+1}\longrightarrow1.$$
At each resolution the discrete operator equals the forward operator and the
discretized datum is formed exactly before adding noise, so the operator,
pre-inversion, and algebraic-solve channels vanish; only data perturbation
remains. Thus vanishing noise alone does not force vanishing reconstruction
error when the retained singular values shrink and $\lambda_n$ is chosen as
above.

items.title: Early stopping leaves a nonzero Tikhonov normal residual
items.statement:
Let $X=Y=\mathbb R$ with the usual inner product, let $A=A_h=I$, let
$x^\dagger=0$, $y=y_{h,\delta}=0$, $e=0$, and set $\lambda=1$. The exact
Tikhonov output is $R_{\lambda,h}y_{h,\delta}=0$, and its normal equation is
$2x=0$. Apply one Richardson step with step size $1/4$ from $x_0=1/2$:
$$\widetilde x_h=x_1=x_0-\frac14(2x_0)=\frac14.$$
The returned output has exact normal-equation residual
$$r_{h,h}=2\widetilde x_h=\frac12\ne0,$$
and reconstruction error $|x^\dagger-\widetilde x_h|=1/4$. The bias, data,
operator, and pre-inversion channels are zero; only the algebraic solve channel
is nonzero.
